youtube.title: Why Sidewalks Have Lines Cut Into Them 🧱 #Shorts #science #facts #didyouknow
youtube.description:
Concrete always cracks as it dries and as temperatures change, because it shrinks and swells. Builders cut or tool grooves called control joints into the slab, creating weak lines so cracking happens along them instead of randomly. The result is tidy, hidden cracks that do not wreck the surface.

Subscribe to The Hidden Why for a new why every day.
